minutes.headline: Finance Committee backed the pared-down FY21 town budget and deferred the capital plan and streetlight article to Town Meeting.
minutes.summary: At a remote public hearing on the warrant articles, the committee heard the town accountant present a revised FY21 budget cut back for COVID-19 revenue uncertainty. It voted recommendations on most articles and deferred the capital plan, streetlights, stabilization, water enterprise and the citizen petition. It also discussed the draft Finance Committee letter and approved prior minutes.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted to recommend the town budget article, which the town accountant had presented in revised, pared-down form for COVID-19 revenue uncertainty.
The committee deferred its recommendation on the FY2021 capital plan to Town Meeting; the pared-down plan is funded only through free cash.
The streetlight purchase article was deferred; the committee will ask the town manager and selectmen to resolve how it is funded.
The Stabilization Fund and water enterprise articles were also deferred, the latter pending an explanation of its revenue source.
Next meeting was set for Thursday May 14 at 7 o'clock, and the May 21 slot was cancelled.

why_it_matters: The budget recommendation shapes what Town Meeting voters are asked to approve for FY21, and the deferred capital plan and streetlight articles leave open how free cash is used and whether the town takes on the cost of owning its streetlights.
